12.03.2024 SA No.155 of 2022 
Hon’ble Alok Kumar Verma, J.
The proposed Second Appeal has been 
filed along with an Application to condone the 
delay of 5749 days. 
2. Heard Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, learned 
counsel for the proposed appellants and Mr. 
R.P. Nautiyal, learned Senior Advocate, assisted 
by Ms. Garima Thapa, learned counsel for 
respondent no.1-Rajendra Singh on Delay 
Condonation Application (IA No.2 of 2022)
3. Notice has been served on respondent 
no.2. 
4. A cross Second Appeal has been filed by 
respondent no.1. The said Second Appeal (SA 
No.8 of 2005) is still pending. 
5. Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, Advocate, 
appearing for the proposed appellants,
submitted that the appellants’ father was 
contesting the Second Appeal No.8 of 2005 as a 
sole respondent. Respondent-Mangal Singh, 
father of the appellants, died on 16.02.2020. 
Thereafter, the present proposed appellants
were substituted in Second Appeal No.8 of 
2005. Then, it has come to the knowledge to 
the proposed appellants that the appellants are 
required to file a Second Appeal. 
6. Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, Senior Advocate, 
contended that the delay has not been properly 
explained.  7. The rules of the procedure are made to 
advance the cause of justice and not to defeat 
it.
8. Having regard to the totality of the facts 
and circumstances of the case, this Court is 
inclined to hold that the cause shown by the 
proposed appellants for condoning the delay in 
filing the Second Appeal, is a sufficient cause 
within the meaning of Section 5 of the 
Limitation Act, 1963.
9. Therefore, the application filed for delay 
condonation deserves to be condoned. The 
Delay Condonation Application (2 of 2022) is 
allowed. Delay is condoned. 
10. List along with SA No.8 of 2005 on 
21.03.2024 for argument on Admission. 
 (Alok Kumar Verma, J.) 
 12.03.2024
Shiv/

In
SA No. 155 of 2022
Hon’ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. J.K. Pandey, holding brief of Mr. Piyush Garg, 
learned counsel for the appellants.
2. Mr. R.P. Nautiyal, learned Sr. Advocate, assisted by 
Mr. Pavan Kumar Nath, learned counsel for the 
respondents.
3. There was the delay of 5749 days in filing the instant 
second appeal, which was condoned by this Court on 
12.03.2024. Against the order dated 12.03.2024, respondents 
filed a Special Leave to Appeal before the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court, which was disposed of by the Hon’ble Supreme 
Court on 18.11.2014 with the following directions:
 
 “While we are not inclined to interfere with the order 
passed by the High Court condoning the delay of 5749 
days in filing the second appeal, we direct the respondents 
to pay costs quantified at Rs. 50,000/- (Rupees Fifty 
Thousand Only) to the appellant herein within a period of 
three months from today.” 
4. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that in 
compliance of the Hon’ble Supreme Court’s order, a 
demand draft of Rs. 50,000/- was sent through post to the 
respondents but the same was refused and thereafter, 
original demand draft is placed on record by way of 
application (I.A. No. 4 of 2025).
5. Learned counsel for the respondents submits that the 
validity period of demand draft was 3 months, and as such, 
the same is expired now. 
6. In such an eventuality, appellant is directed to place a
fresh demand draft or get the demand draft renewed within 
a week. 
7. Registry is directed to return back the demand draft 
to the learned counsel for the appellants. 
8. List on 25.06.2025.
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 12.06.2025.
SKS

38 UKHC010002682005
SA No. 155 of 2022
Sarjeet Singh Rana and others .…… Appellants
Vs. 
Rajendra Singh and another ……Respondents
Hon’ble Ravindra Maithani, J.
Dr. A.K. Gautam, Advocate for the 
appellants through video conferencing.
Mr. Pawan Kumar Nath and Mr. A.M. 
Saklani, Advocates for the respondent no.1.
Heard.
Instant appeal is admitted on the 
following substantial questions of law:-
(i) Whether Rajendra Singh 
(respondent no.1) has any locus 
standi to challenge the registered 
sale deed executed by his father 
Kripal Singh during his lifetime?
(ii) Whether non-challenge of registered 
sale deed by Late Smt. Tara Devi 
during her lifetime for 23 years 
amounts to giving consent by way of 
her conduct to Kripal Singh for 
selling her share of land?
 LCR has already been received.
 In fact, the same impugned judgment is 
challenged in Second Appeal No. 8 of 2005. It 
is almost 21 years when one of the connected 
appeals was filed.
 List on 21.08.2026 for final hearing 
alongwith connected matter.
 No adjournment from any side may be 
entertained on the date fixed.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.) 
 03.07.2026
Jitendra
